items.stem: When determining whether a worker is an employee or an independent contractor, the key consideration is:

options.text: The degree of control and the nature of the working relationship
options.rationale: Correct: classification rests on control and relationship facts, not labels.
A title alone does not determine status.

options.text: Whether the worker has a business card
options.rationale: A business card is irrelevant to classification.

items.explanation: Correct: classification rests on control and relationship facts, not labels.

items.stem: A payroll register must be reconciled to the general ledger primarily to:

options.text: Ensure recorded payroll matches amounts actually paid and posted
options.rationale: Correct: reconciliation catches discrepancies between payroll and the ledger.
Reconciliation complements controls, not replaces them.

items.explanation: Correct: reconciliation catches discrepancies between payroll and the ledger.

items.stem: Select TWO controls that help prevent fraudulent or duplicate payroll payments.

options.text: Segregation of duties between setup and payment approval
options.rationale: Correct: separating duties limits single-person fraud.

options.text: Reconciling the payroll register before disbursement
options.rationale: Correct: reconciliation catches duplicates and errors.

options.text: Letting one person both add employees and release pay
Skipping all reviews to save time
options.rationale: No review removes a key control.
Audit logs support detection, not removal.

items.explanation: Correct: separating duties limits single-person fraud. Correct: reconciliation catches duplicates and errors.
